paragraphs.title: God as the Source of Strength and Protection

easy.explanation: David says that the LORD teaches his hands to war and his fingers to fight.

answers: As his source of goodness and protection
easy.explanation: David calls the LORD his goodness, fortress, high tower, deliverer, and shield.
easy.q: How does David describe the LORD in these verses?

easy.explanation: David says that the LORD is the one in whom he trusts.
easy.q: In whom does David say he trusts?

answers: Because the LORD teaches him to fight and protects him
Because the LORD gives him riches only
Because the LORD commands him to sing
medium.explanation: David blesses the LORD for teaching him to fight and for being his protector.
medium.q: Why does David bless the LORD at the beginning of the psalm?

medium.explanation: A fortress is a strong defensive place, fitting the other protective titles in the verse.
medium.q: What does the word “fortress” suggest in verse 2?

answers: Teacher in battle, protector, deliverer, and shield
medium.explanation: The verses present the LORD as David’s teacher, fortress, deliverer, and shield.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the LORD’s roles for David?

answers: David depends only on his own strength
The LORD gives David ability to act and also provides refuge
David wants to leave the battle
challenge.explanation: The LORD both trains David for battle and protects him from danger.
challenge.q: What connection is made between learning to fight and the descriptions of protection?

answers: Who subdueth my people under me
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the LORD bringing David’s people under his rule.
challenge.q: Which phrase shows that the LORD actively rules over David’s people?

answers: The many ways God supports and protects David
A change to a different subject
challenge.explanation: The titles present several aspects of God’s care, protection, and deliverance.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the many titles given to the LORD in verse 2?

paragraphs.title: Human Frailty and a Prayer for Divine Intervention

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that man’s days are as a shadow that passeth away.
easy.q: How are the days of man described?

answers: Bow the heavens and come down
easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do from heaven?

easy.explanation: He asks to be delivered from the hand of strange children.
easy.q: From whom does the psalmist ask to be delivered?

answers: Because human life is brief and passing
medium.explanation: After describing human weakness and the brevity of life, he asks the LORD to act and save him.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask for divine intervention after describing man?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to foreign enemies from whom the psalmist seeks deliverance.
medium.q: What does “strange children” mean in this passage?

answers: Singing, building houses, and raising flocks
The LORD coming down, scattering enemies, and delivering him
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks God to come down, defeat the enemies, and deliver him from them.
medium.q: Which order correctly describes the psalmist’s request?

answers: Human frailty and passing life versus the LORD’s great power
challenge.explanation: Man is described as weak and temporary, while the LORD is asked to act powerfully from heaven.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in this passage?

answers: Their words and actions are unreliable
challenge.explanation: Vanity and falsehood show that the enemies cannot be trusted.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the enemies’ mouths speaking vanity and their right hands being false?

answers: Through lightning, arrows, and a hand sent from above
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks for lightning, arrows, and God’s hand from above to defeat the enemies.
challenge.q: How do the requested acts of intervention display God’s power?

easy.explanation: David says, “I will sing a new song unto thee.”
easy.q: What kind of song does David promise to sing to the LORD?

answers: A psaltery and an instrument of ten strings
easy.explanation: David mentions a psaltery and an instrument of ten strings.
easy.q: With what instrument does David say he will praise the LORD?

answers: The hurtful sword and strange children
easy.explanation: The LORD delivers David from the hurtful sword and from the hand of strange children.
easy.q: From what does the LORD deliver David?

medium.explanation: The new song expresses gratitude for the LORD’s deliverance.
medium.q: Why does David want to sing a new song?

medium.explanation: The context shows that the LORD rescues David from the sword and his enemies.
medium.q: What does “delivereth” mean in this passage?

answers: The song responds to recognition that the LORD saves David
The song concerns a subject unrelated to God
The later verses cancel the request for deliverance
medium.explanation: David sings to the LORD while acknowledging that the LORD gives salvation and delivers him.
medium.q: What connection exists between verse 9 and verses 10–11?

answers: Victory is credited to God, not merely to royal strength
challenge.explanation: The verse presents God as the source of salvation even for kings.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the statement that God gives salvation unto kings?

challenge.explanation: Both passages mention being delivered from strange children.
challenge.q: What detail appears both in the previous passage and here?

challenge.explanation: After deliverance, David responds with praise and thanksgiving.
challenge.q: What does the movement from a request for deliverance to singing suggest?

answers: As plants grown up in their youth
easy.explanation: The verse compares the sons to plants grown up in their youth.
The psalm says, “That our garners may be full.”
easy.q: What is described as being full?

answers: Having the LORD as their God
easy.explanation: The psalm concludes that happy are the people whose God is the LORD.
easy.q: What is identified as the highest happiness of the people?

medium.explanation: The passage describes full garners and sheep bringing forth thousands and ten thousands.
medium.q: Which combination best describes abundance in these verses?

answers: They are flourishing and well developed
medium.explanation: The comparison presents the sons as growing and flourishing.
medium.q: What does “grown up” communicate about the plants used as a comparison?

answers: Quiet, secure streets express peace and blessing
medium.explanation: The absence of breaking in, going out, and complaining portrays a peaceful society.
medium.q: How do the streets relate to the conclusion of the psalm?

answers: Personal and material blessings are presented as part of the happiness of the whole people
Prosperity is the source of danger
challenge.explanation: The passage gathers many blessings together and ends with the happiness of the entire people.
challenge.q: What does the movement from family and prosperity to “happy is that people” teach?

answers: Sons, daughters, garners, flocks, oxen, and streets
A psaltery and a new song
challenge.explanation: The description includes family, property, animals, work, and public spaces.
challenge.q: Which group describes a whole society rather than one individual?

answers: There is no invasion or loss in the community
There are no storehouses in the settlement
There are no people in the nation
challenge.explanation: The absence of breaking in or going out suggests security and freedom from loss.
challenge.q: What is the connection between “no breaking in, nor going out” and the peace described?
